question: With reference to Anak Krakatau, which erupted strongly in September 2026, consider the following statements:
statements: It lies on the Sunda Arc, formed by the subduction of the Indo-Australian Plate beneath the Sunda Plate.
The December 2018 tsunami linked to it was generated by a lateral flank collapse rather than by a tectonic earthquake.
It sits in the Strait of Malacca between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.
tail: How many of the statements are correct?
explanation: Only two. Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Sunda Arc, Indo-Australian Plate subducting beneath the Sunda Plate; the 2018 tsunami came from a flank collapse, not an earthquake). Statement 3 is wrong — Anak Krakatau lies in the Sunda Strait (between Java and Sumatra), not the Strait of Malacca.
subject: Current Affairs

question: ISRO hot-tested the Power Head Test Article (PHTA) of its semi-cryogenic engine at full 200-tonne thrust in September 2026. Which of the following about the SCE-200 is/are correct?
statements: It burns refined kerosene (ISROSENE) with liquid oxygen.
It uses an oxidiser-rich staged combustion cycle.
It is intended to replace the L110 core stage of the LVM3.
explanation: 1, 2 and 3. The SCE-200 burns ISROSENE (refined kerosene) with liquid oxygen, uses oxidiser-rich staged combustion, and is meant to replace the LVM3's L110 core and power the NGLV.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The National Policy on Geothermal Energy and India's first geothermal wells were in the news this week. India's first two geothermal wells have been commissioned at:
explanation: Puga Valley, eastern Ladakh. India's first two geothermal wells were commissioned there in July 2026; the National Policy on Geothermal Energy (MNRE) was notified 15 September 2025.
subject: Current Affairs

question: UNEP's first dedicated "Limiting Overshoot" report (September 2026) is best described by which framing?

options.text: That 1.5 °C can still be avoided entirely if emissions peak by 2030
That warming is likely to cross 1.5 °C in the next few years, with a return possible under an "overshoot, peak and decline" pathway
That carbon dioxide removal alone can safely return the world below 1.5 °C regardless of peak warming
That end-of-century warming, not peak warming, determines the physical damage caused

explanation: UNEP says 1.5 °C will likely be crossed within a few years but a return is possible under an "overshoot, peak and decline" pathway; peak warming (not end-of-century) drives the damage, and CDR can return the world below 1.5 °C only if peak stays well below 2 °C.
subject: Current Affairs

question: From 4 September 2026, NPCI's masking mandate took effect for UPI. Which statement is correct?

options.text: UPI apps must now display the full registered mobile number to build counterparty trust.
Only the last four digits of the registered mobile number may be shown to the counterparty.
The mandate was issued as a statutory rule under the DPDP Act, 2023.
Virtual Payment Addresses (VPAs) are exempted from the masking requirement.

explanation: Only the last four digits of the mobile number may be shown; VPAs and account numbers are also masked. It was issued as an NPCI network circular, not a statute.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The MHA this week floated a draft Article 371(K) for Ladakh. Consider the following:
statements: It proposes a directly elected governing body with legislative powers for the Union Territory of Ladakh.
It would be inserted as a special provision in Part XXI of the Constitution.
At present the President legislates for Ladakh by regulation under Article 240.
explanation: 1, 2 and 3. All three are correct: a directly elected legislative body for UT Ladakh, a new special provision in Part XXI, and the current position that the President legislates for Ladakh under Article 240.
subject: Current Affairs

question: ISRO's GSLV-F17 / EOS-05 mission was praised by the PM this week. What made EOS-05 notable?

options.text: It is India's first satellite launched from a foreign spaceport.
It is India's first-ever imaging satellite placed in a geosynchronous orbit.
It is India's first satellite in a sun-synchronous polar orbit.
It is India's first reusable Earth-observation platform.

explanation: EOS-05 is India's first imaging satellite in a geosynchronous orbit (~36,000 km), giving continuous "staring" coverage of the subcontinent, unlike the usual polar/sun-synchronous remote-sensing satellites.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) cleared Acceptances of Necessity (AoN) worth about Rs 1.10 lakh crore this week. Which statement is correct?

options.text: An AoN represents the signing of a procurement contract with a selected vendor.
The DAC is chaired by the Chief of Defence Staff.
An AoN is the "in-principle" approval that begins the procurement, not the contract itself.

explanation: An AoN is the DAC's in-principle approval that *begins* procurement — not the contract. The DAC is chaired by the Defence Minister (not the CDS), and "Buy (Indian-IDDM)" is the topmost priority category under DAP 2020.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Boma–Badingilo Migratory Landscape, in the news this week, is associated with which country and distinction?

options.text: Kenya — home of the Serengeti wildebeest migration
South Sudan — its first UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed via emergency procedure and placed on the In-Danger list simultaneously
Tanzania — a newly delisted natural World Heritage Site

explanation: Boma–Badingilo (South Sudan) — its first UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed via emergency procedure and simultaneously placed on the List of World Heritage in Danger; it hosts the Great Nile Migration.
subject: Current Affairs

question: ORV *Sagar Manthan*, launched this week, is best described as:

options.text: India's first domestically built advanced ocean research vessel, built by GRSE for NCPOR under the Ministry of Earth Sciences
A polar icebreaker acquired from Russia
A deep-sea manned submersible under the Samudrayaan mission

explanation: ORV *Sagar Manthan* — India's first domestically built advanced ocean research vessel, built by GRSE (Kolkata) for NCPOR under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
subject: Current Affairs

question: At the 25th SCO Summit whose Bishkek Declaration featured this week, which procedural change was decided?

options.text: India was admitted as a new full member.
English was adopted as a working language of the SCO, alongside Russian and Chinese.
The SCO Secretariat was relocated from Beijing to Bishkek.
The grouping was renamed the Eurasian Economic Union.

explanation: The Bishkek Declaration adopted English as a working language of the SCO, alongside Russian and Chinese.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The PM-KUSUM 2.0 scheme, previewed this week, is notable for a dedicated component of about 10 GW in:
explanation: PM-KUSUM 2.0 is expected to carry a dedicated agri-photovoltaics component of about 10 GW — solar generation over cultivated cropland.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Consider the following about the Pacific Ring of Fire:
statements: It is a horseshoe-shaped belt marked by frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions around the Pacific Ocean.
It is associated primarily with divergent (constructive) plate boundaries.
The Andes and the Cascade Range lie along it.
explanation: 1 and 3 only. The Ring of Fire is a horseshoe belt of intense seismic/volcanic activity round the Pacific, along convergent (subduction) boundaries — not divergent — so statement 2 is wrong. The Andes and Cascades lie along it.
subject: Geography

question: Which of the following correctly pairs an Indian soil type with a characteristic feature?
statements: Black soil (regur) — rich in iron, lime and magnesia; retains moisture; ideal for cotton.
Laterite soil — formed by intense leaching in high-rainfall tropical areas; poor in lime.
Alluvial soil — the most widespread soil, generally deficient in phosphorus and humus in older (bhangar) tracts.
explanation: 1, 2 and 3. All three pairings are correct.
subject: Geography

question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
explanation: Odisha. The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states — Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram — but not Odisha.
subject: Geography

question: With reference to the Indian monsoon, consider the following:
statements: The southwest monsoon sets in over Kerala normally around the first week of June.
The "burst" of the monsoon is associated with the sudden onset of heavy rain.
The retreating monsoon brings most of the annual rainfall to the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu).
explanation: 1, 2 and 3. All three are correct: Kerala onset ~1 June, the "burst," and the retreating (northeast) monsoon feeding the Coromandel Coast in Oct–Dec.
subject: Geography

question: Which one of the following rivers is a west-flowing river that drains into the Arabian Sea?
explanation: Narmada. The Narmada (like the Tapi) flows west into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley; Mahanadi, Krishna and Godavari are east-flowing to the Bay of Bengal.
subject: Geography

question: Consider the following mountain passes and their locations:
statements: Nathu La — Sikkim
Zoji La — Jammu & Kashmir / Ladakh
Bomdila — Arunachal Pradesh
tail: How many pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: All three. Nathu La (Sikkim), Zoji La (J&K/Ladakh) and Bomdila (Arunachal Pradesh) are all correctly matched.
subject: Geography

question: The phenomenon of El Niño is generally associated with:

options.text: Abnormal warming of surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, often linked to weaker Indian monsoon rainfall
Abnormal cooling of the eastern Pacific, strengthening the Indian monsoon
A permanent warm current off the coast of Peru unrelated to atmospheric circulation
Enhanced upwelling of cold water along the South American coast

explanation: El Niño is the abnormal warming of the central/eastern equatorial Pacific; it is generally associated with weaker/deficient Indian monsoon rainfall.
subject: Geography

question: Which of the following correctly describes the Deccan Trap?

options.text: A belt of folded sedimentary mountains formed during the Himalayan orogeny
An extensive plateau of basaltic lava flows formed by fissure volcanism, associated with the black-soil region
A region of ancient metamorphic rocks forming the oldest part of the Himalayas
A coastal alluvial plain built by the deposition of peninsular rivers

explanation: The Deccan Trap is an extensive basaltic-lava plateau formed by fissure (flood) volcanism, weathering into the black regur soil of the region.
subject: Geography
